machines.name: 808-style
machines.tagline: Booming analog kick, snappy snare, metallic hats
machines.description: Analog-modelled voices in the spirit of the 1980 classic: resonator kick with a long tuned tail, two-tone snare with noise, six-oscillator metallic hats and cymbal, multi-burst clap, cowbell, congas and clave.

machines.name: 909-style
machines.tagline: Punchy kick with click, noisy snare, gritty hats
machines.description: Hybrid analog/digital style: kick with a fast pitch drop and beater click, noise-heavy snares, tuned toms, and crunchy low-bit-depth hats, crash and ride.

machines.name: 707-style
machines.tagline: Crisp digital drums with an 8-bit edge
machines.description: Punchy, sample-like voices with short, natural envelopes and a gentle early-digital crunch: two kicks, two snares, toms, rim, cowbell, clap, tambourine, hats, crash and ride.

machines.name: 606-style
machines.description: Lean analog voices: short tight kick, bright noisy snare, very tight metallic hats and a splashy cymbal, plus a few companions (clap, rim, shaker, zap) in the same thin style.

machines.name: LinnDrum-style
machines.description: Acoustic-modelled drums with the companded 8-bit sheen of early-80s sample machines: dry punchy kick, fat snare, sidestick, real-sounding claps, hats, ride, crash, toms, congas, cabasa, tambourine and cowbell.

machines.name: CR-78-style
machines.description: Gentle, rounded voices from the preset rhythm-box era: soft resonant kick and snare, ticking hats, guiro, maracas, tambourine, bongos, congas, clave, cowbell and the metallic "metal beat".

manifest.name: TR-808 Recordings
manifest.description: 116 one-shots recorded directly from a real Roland TR-808 (serial no. 103852) by Michael Fischer of Technopolis in 1994: 25 bass drums and 25 snares across the tone/decay and tone/snappy knobs, 25 cymbals, toms, congas, open hats and every other voice, each from its individual output at 16-bit/44.1 kHz. The '808 Classic' kit puts all 16 instruments on the pads; '808 Boom' keeps the essentials on bank A and plays the long-decay bass drum as a tuned 808 bass on bank B (C minor scale, pads choke each other). File names follow the original knob positions, e.g. bd0010 = tone 0, decay 10 (see README.md).
manifest.author: Michael Fischer (Technopolis)
manifest.attribution: TR-808 samples by Michael Fischer / Technopolis (1994), via tidalcycles/sounds-tr808-fischer (CC0 1.0).

items.name: uzu Drumkit
items.description: A small, carefully made electronic kit from the TidalCycles community: synthesized drums by Switch Angel run through an LA-76-style compressor, and modular-synth blips recorded by Ludens and Switch Angel. Kit A is a full electronic kit with alternate hats, kicks and percussion on bank B; Kit B swaps in alternate kicks and snares and puts the modular hits on pads 13–16. Not included: the upstream processed Amen break, the samples contributed by Mot4i (published elsewhere with an attribution request, not under the repo's Unlicense) and two unattributed acoustic files.

items.name: Sonic Pi Drums & Percussion
items.description: The drum and percussion part of the sample library that ships with Sonic Pi: an acoustic kit (kicks, snares, hats, cymbals and toms at two dynamics), 15 kicks, 22 hats, 4 snares, 25 electronic blips and hits, finger snaps and 26 tabla strokes. Collected from freesound.org and donated sounds, all dedicated to the public domain (CC0); the bundled README.md links every original. Four kits: Acoustic, Electro, Kick & Hat Lab (8 kicks on bank A, 8 hats on bank B) and Tabla.

items.name: FreePats Synth Percussion
items.description: 21 drum sounds created by Roberto (FreePats project) with the Yoshimi and Geonkick software synthesizers as an approximation of drum sounds from vintage electronic music made with analog synths: kicks, snares, hats, claps, claves, toms, shakers and long cymbals. One 16-pad kit; the second take of each tom is in the folder for variation.
